plan_summary: Install and configure Nginx on Ubuntu 24.04 by updating system packages, adding the official repository key if necessary, installing the package, verifying the service status, and configuring basic security settings.
assumptions: The host has internet access to download packages.
The user has sudo privileges to install software.

tasks.title: Update system package lists and upgrade existing packages
tasks.objective: Ensure the local package index is current before installing new software.
tasks.rationale: Running apt update prevents installation of outdated versions and resolves dependency conflicts early in the process.
tasks.expected_output: Command completes with a summary of packages that can be upgraded or are already up to date.
success_criteria: The command exits with status code 0.
No critical errors are reported in the output.

tasks.title: Add Nginx official GPG key and repository (if not present)
tasks.objective: Ensure the system can access the latest stable Nginx packages from the official source.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 repositories may contain older versions; adding the official key ensures security patches are available.
tasks.expected_output: The GPG key is added to /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/ and the repository source list is updated.
success_criteria: The apt command reports 'No changes' if already configured, or successfully adds the new source.

tasks.title: Install Nginx package and dependencies
tasks.objective: Download and install the Nginx web server software.
tasks.rationale: This is the core installation step that places binaries, libraries, and configuration files onto the system.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx package is installed with default configuration files in /etc/nginx/.
success_criteria: The command exits with status code 0.

tasks.title: Start and enable the Nginx service
tasks.objective: Launch the Nginx daemon and configure it to start automatically on boot.
tasks.rationale: Installation alone does not run the server; the systemd unit must be started and enabled for persistence.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx process is running in the foreground or managed by systemd, and the service is marked as 'enabled'.

tasks.title: Verify Nginx is listening on port 80
tasks.objective: Confirm the web server is accepting connections on the standard HTTP port.
tasks.rationale: Ensures the service is bound to the correct interface and port as expected for a web server.
tasks.expected_output: Output confirms listening sockets on 0.0.0.0:80 or 127.0.0.1:80.
success_criteria: The netstat/ss command lists port 80 as LISTEN.

tasks.title: Test HTTP connectivity to the server
tasks.objective: Validate that a client can successfully retrieve content from the Nginx instance.
tasks.rationale: Functional testing confirms DNS resolution (if applicable), port accessibility, and basic request handling.
tasks.expected_output: A successful HTTP response (e.g., 'Welcome to nginx!') is returned.
success_criteria: curl returns a 200 OK status code.

tasks.title: Review and secure default configuration files
tasks.objective: Inspect the default site configuration to ensure no sensitive data is exposed.
tasks.rationale: Default configurations often expose server versions or directory listings that should be hardened.
tasks.expected_output: A list of identified security risks in the default config files (e.g., version disclosure).

tasks.title: Configure basic security headers in default site
tasks.objective: Add security headers like X-Frame-Options and Content-Security-Policy to the default server block.
tasks.rationale: Prevents clickjacking, MIME type sniffing, and other common web vulnerabilities by default.
tasks.expected_output: Updated configuration file containing security headers in the server block.

tasks.title: Restart Nginx to apply security changes
tasks.objective: Reload or restart the service to incorporate configuration updates without downtime.
tasks.rationale: Changes made to configuration files require a reload/restart to take effect immediately.
tasks.expected_output: Service restarts successfully and logs show configuration test passed.
success_criteria: systemctl status nginx shows 'active (running)' after restart.

tasks.title: Document installation steps and verify final state
tasks.objective: Create a summary of the installation process and confirm all success criteria are met.
tasks.rationale: Documentation aids future maintenance, troubleshooting, and audit compliance.
tasks.expected_output: A brief report confirming Nginx is installed, running, secured, and accessible.
success_criteria: All previous tasks (T01-T09) have passed their success criteria.
